items.decision: The 7 investigations stand as the ground for this design, although each is partial for the reasons listed.
items.evidence: You accepted, with the note "gap accepted".

items.decision: The system shape is inherited: skills run by an agent in the current session, plus scripts and the existing adapters; no new process, and the bug pipeline's detached fixer goes.
No new skill: diagnose stays a utility where it is, fix stays the small-lane skill, and to-ticket gains a bug and ad-hoc mode.
The in-place fix is a shared fix procedure file in the fix skill's folder, read by the fix skill and the 5 in-place callers; the fix skill runs standalone only.
The diagnosis file is the hand-off: diagnose writes it, fix reads it by path and passes the same path to the to-ticket bug mode.
The to-ticket bug mode reaches the tracker through the tracker adapter verbs, from one new script, on Jira and GitHub Issues alike.
A defect outside the slice that blocks it: the executing agent runs the standalone fix itself in a second worktree it owns, made from the base branch, then continues its slice.
The executor carries the fix to its feature branch by cherry-picking the fix commit after the fix's own change is open.
The feature's change names the fix's change as a dependency in a managed block of its description, and the fix's ticket gets a comment linking both.
The surfaces other people call, as packeted in round 1: the 3 skill invocations, the shared fix procedure file, the removed bug skill, and the adapter verbs used (none added).
INV-008 to INV-010 stand as the ground for round 2, although each is partial.

The diagnosis is one file, DIAGNOSIS.md, in the bug's own spec folder, committed with the failing test on a local diagnosis branch made from the base branch and never pushed by diagnose; a fix continues on that branch.
A bug with no ticket gets a provisional work id; once the ticket exists, the bug mode asks for the spec folder again with the key and moves the folder if the path differs.
Proof is attached to the ticket only; no proof is committed to git.
items.evidence: You reversed to the attachment option, with the note "no proof to be git committed. only attached to ticket".

items.decision: Proof stays on the ticket, text and images and any other file, never in git. The diagnosis file merges with the fix and stays, as recommended; your answer did not mention it.
items.evidence: You wrote in: "the proof stays in the ticket (text, images, and whatnot), not git".

items.decision: The bug mode sets one named state, in review, through jira.transitions and state-labels; the code starts reading jira.transitions and 3 documents are corrected.
The diagnosis file lists every outside write already done, and each evidence comment carries a visible marker.
Approval is enforced by the skill text alone; no script checks it.
The bug mode takes any ticket key it is given.
items.evidence: You reversed to the option that takes any ticket key.

items.decision: A failed outside write may be retried, but before each retry the run checks whether the earlier attempt took effect.
items.evidence: You reversed to the retry option, with the note "as long as before retrying, check if the previous supposedly failed attempt actually produce something that we should not do again".

items.decision: Proof carries no credentials, using the credential rules of the existing redaction script, shared.
Writes run as the developer; no new log and no feature flag.
Signed, then void: your answers to the proof, retention and approval cards in the same send changed what the packet described. It comes back below with the changes marked.
Signed, then void: your approval and ticket-key answers in the same send changed what the packet described. It comes back below with the changes marked.
INV-011 stands as the ground for round 3, although it is partial. Its outside fact, that GitHub has no upload, turned out wrong; see the correction in round 4.
Images on GitHub Issues go on the ticket, since you asked me to check and GitHub does support it, through its command-line tool. Text only applies only where that upload is not available.
items.evidence: You wrote in: "I do not know but I don't think Github does not support images upload to issue (seems like a very basic necessity), so please verify. if it's truly not supported, then text only and devs attach files manually". GitHub CLI 2.99.0 uploads images and videos: docs.github.com/en/github-cli/github-cli/attaching-files-with-github-cli

items.decision: The tracker adapter family gains one verb, attach; Jira sends the file's real type. Its line saying GitHub Issues answers unsupported is replaced in round 4.
Before each retry, the run reads back whether the failed write took effect. At most 2 retries, after 5 and 20 seconds. A write with no read-back is not retried.
The diagnosis file keeps an approval section: who, their words or the prior approval, what it covers, the date. Nothing checks it.
A given ticket key gets the write. It is recorded if the diagnosis file has no key yet, else listed with the outside writes.
The executor reads the change's description before it rewrites the dependency block.
Signed, then void: its GitHub proof row said images need a manual drag, which the check of your Q-4 answer proved wrong. It comes back below.
Signed, then void: its attach row said GitHub Issues answers unsupported, which the same check proved wrong. It comes back below.
Signed: who is let through.
GitHub's own documentation stands as the ground for uploading images to GitHub Issues; the first live run happens when the upload is built.
On GitHub Issues, attach posts the evidence comment with each image or video inline through gh; any other file is named for the developer to add.
A retried GitHub Issues attach first reads the ticket's comments for the evidence marker.
The dependency register requires gh 2.99.0 or later with GitHub Issues; an older gh names the files instead of uploading them.
Signed: what the small lane stores.
Signed: the surfaces other people call.
INV-012 to INV-014 stand as the ground for round 5, although each is partial.
A bug's state is read from the diagnosis file's fields, never stored as its own field.
Each part of the diagnosis file has one writer; the list of outside writes is append-only, written by the bug mode and fix.
A script checks the diagnosis file's required parts, the verdict's evidence and the certainty marks; fix refuses a file that fails.
Running diagnose again rewrites the verdict, root cause and proposal and empties the approval; a steer re-runs diagnose.
Standalone fix order: ticket, local fix, push and Draft change, proof, ticket in review, CI wait, ready and reviewer.
The fix waits for CI in the background like preflight; anything but green leaves the change Draft with the reason.
An agent's verdict on a defect outside its slice decides: fix, ticket and park, park, or ticket and go on.
In a hands-off run, the separate change stays Draft; a person marks it ready.
A fix for a bug reported on a feature branch commits there and pushes, with no ticket and no new change.
Signed, then void: your feature-branch answer in the same send adds a state and a rule. It comes back below.
Signed, then void: your feature-branch answer in the same send adds a push to a shared branch. It comes back below.
Diagnose run off the base branch asks once which branch to start from, and records it.
A feature-branch fix lands by a fast-forward push, never forced; one rebase and full re-test if the branch moved, else it stops.
A feature-branch fix posts its proof on that branch's open change, or in the run's report.
Signed: what the small lane stores.
Signed: the surfaces other people call.
Signed: what the small lane refuses.
Signed: every outside write.
Accepted as ground: the investigations of a new tracker verb and of the skill files, scripts and checks.
No new skill; each new file lives beside the skill that owns it.
The standalone fix's outside writes run from one script with three steps: open, ready, land.
One shared helper is the only code that adds to a diagnosis's list of outside writes, and it runs the read-back before each retry.
The upload verb is tracker_attach: one comment carrying the files; the registry check matches whole verb names.
The shared fix procedure keeps today's results, and every caller handles every result.
The developer settings and their fail-closed rule move to the plugin's configuration document.
New tests go in the main test folder, run in CI on Linux and Windows, against stub trackers and forges.
Dependency direction is the plugin's own; nothing names what calls it.
The check script holds a table of the parts each verdict needs, and works out the bug's state from the fields.
Both outside-writing scripts are a list of named steps; a listed step is skipped, a failed one retried through the helper.
Kind differences between trackers, and between forges, stay inside each adapter.
Accepted as ground: the five seam investigations, partial; the forge and Jira behaviours they could not check live are checked before release.
A red smoke gate is fixed by autopilot between two gate runs, one shared-procedure fix per failing scenario; the gate itself only reports; one re-run, and a second red ends the run red.
Starting a hands-off run is the prior approval for out-of-slice ticket and separate-change writes; merge, force push and ready stay forbidden.
The executor keeps its step numbers and caps; the procedure's results map onto existing statuses, and an out-of-slice design conflict is design_conflict when cited, needs_decision when uncited.
The dependency note lives inside the executor's existing checklist block, and the description is fetched before every rewrite.
The cherry-picked fix carries the bug's work id, not the slice prefix; the second worktree comes from create-worktree; reasons go on the separate change; the slice re-runs from Step 8.
Three new journal events and one autopilot report line for tickets written, separate changes and parked defects.
The procedure re-runs a failure once before diagnosing, and adds a seventh result: flaky.
The procedure records the caller, the input and the failing path from the reproduction.
Diagnose keeps its trace-the-path heading word for word, its investigate and rationale reads, its name, description and language pointer; the dead hand-off is dropped.
Lesson-capture pointers move to the shared procedure file; workflow feedback uses the slice or finding id.
The grills accept a DIAGNOSIS.md as input; grill-solution runs without a PRD; the size call names fix only as a bounce target.
Fix retires the diagnosis worktree through remove-worktree; names are lower-cased and the base fetched; a branch-pattern refusal asks the person, or parks needs_decision in a hands-off run.
The Jira adapter turns markdown into Atlassian Document Format for create, comment and attach; attach embeds media.
One in-review key on both trackers, given as name or id, checked against the ticket's transitions, refused when unconfigured; Jira refuses an unknown fix version; the scaffold key is renamed.
A missing assignee or reviewer is asked for when a person is present; a hands-off run leaves it unassigned and reports it; the literal none means unset.
With tracker or forge set to none, that is found before the first write; the fix then stays local and stops.

The ship script opens the change before posting reasons, routes the CI wait on exit code and output, refuses an empty id and a protected target; landing fetches, checks fast-forward and sets upstream.

To-ticket bug mode files only from a file on disk, never imports the PRD publisher, writes comments or its own region only, keeps the dry-run and the old bug publisher's safeguards, and names the gh 2.99.0 prerequisite.
The bug skill goes in one commit with its manifests, test and every reference; the reviewer setting and change-reviewers land with fix's ready step.
adr/0008 supersedes ADR-0001; report-issue stays a separate egress.
A new commit check refuses /afk:bug and /afk-toolkit:bug mentions outside the changelog and spec folders.
The glossary commit goes with the PRD; the eight bug-pipeline terms and One-live-fixer are removed.
A major release, the bump being yours; a Migration line; the to-demo-plan and settle-mr aliases are removed.
A feature-branch fix lands through the feature's Draft change; one SAFETY sentence, no BEHAVIORS change.
Signed: what existing callers, stored records and flows see differently; compatibility; rollback by pinning the previous plugin version.
Accepted as ground: the five closing investigations; the tickets-and-tracker one re-closes on this round's answers.
A flaky result counts as passed for that run; the caller writes one journal line naming the check and both runs; no new executor status.
A ticket the bug mode creates gets the diagnosis summary as its description; on an existing ticket it writes comments only.
Diagnose's one-line description is rewritten; its trace-the-path heading, name and language pointer stay word for word.
A grill that sends a bug back as still small records the call in its own section of the grill log in one new row shape; fix reads it before changing code.
A solution grill without a requirements document ends at the size call: small goes back to fix, too big goes to the requirements grill.
The requirements' in-place return is served by the shared fix procedure file.
The three new journal events use the existing park form, a subject the dashboard does not join to a slice, and never the word pushed for the separate change.
The journal's park reasons gain several possible fixes, requirements gap and cannot reproduce for defects outside a slice.
The only-the-executor-commits rule widens to the fix helpers autopilot and preflight run.
Jira uploads are read back for stored name and type; file names carry the diagnosis id.
Spinoff tickets on Jira become formatted and refuse an unknown fix version.
The GitLab adapter adds a reviewer instead of replacing the list.
Fix looks its change up by number once opened; several GitLab changes on one branch stop the run.
Unavailable, or an empty created key, counts as a failed write.
Fix creates its worktree in the owned mode, retires it from outside, and reads the remove script's report.
None means unset for reviewer and assignee; the settings keep their K1 to K5 ids.
